title: MCP Server Compliance Test Rules
description: Machine-readable catalog of compliance test rules for MCP servers. Rules are grouped by the MCP specification revision they apply to (specVersion); ids are only comparable within one revision.

categories.name: Transport Validation
categories.description: Streamable HTTP and stdio transport compliance at the wire level

categories.name: Lifecycle & Protocol
categories.description: Connection setup (initialize handshake or per-request _meta plus server/discover), capabilities, and protocol compliance

categories.name: Tool Operations
categories.description: Tool listing, calling, caching hints, and pagination

categories.name: Resource Operations
categories.description: Resource listing, reading, templates, caching hints, pagination, and subscriptions

categories.name: Prompt Operations
categories.description: Prompt listing, retrieval, caching hints, and pagination

categories.name: Error Handling
categories.description: JSON-RPC error responses and error codes
categories.scope: always runs (some rules capability-gated on tools)

categories.name: Schema Validation
categories.description: Structural validation of tool, resource, and prompt definitions and of every recorded server message
categories.scope: capability-gated for definition checks; post-hoc recording scans always run

categories.name: Security Validation
categories.description: Authentication, input validation, tool integrity, and information disclosure tests
categories.scope: runs after all functional tests (input validation and tool integrity rules capability-gated on tools)

rules.name: HTTP POST accepted
rules.description: Verifies the server accepts HTTP POST requests with JSON-RPC payloads
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 2xx response for POST with JSON-RPC body
rules.failCriteria: Non-2xx response

rules.name: Responds with JSON or SSE
rules.description: Verifies the server responds with a valid Content-Type header
rules.passCriteria: Content-Type includes application/json or text/event-stream
rules.failCriteria: Content-Type is neither application/json nor text/event-stream

rules.name: Rejects non-JSON request Content-Type
rules.description: Sends POST with Content-Type: text/plain and verifies server rejects it
rules.passCriteria: Server returns 4xx for non-application/json Content-Type (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After); any other 403 counts only when the same ping sent as application/json (a 429 on it retried once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429), whatever its message says
rules.failCriteria: Server accepts request with incorrect Content-Type; a 5xx; not evaluable when a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place, or its application/json twin drew the same 403 (quoted when its message names Host/Origin validation), a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: GET returns SSE stream or 405
rules.description: Verifies the server handles GET requests appropriately
rules.passCriteria: Returns 405, text/event-stream, or any 2xx response
rules.failCriteria: Returns a non-2xx, non-405 response

rules.name: DELETE accepted or returns 405
rules.description: Verifies the server handles DELETE requests appropriately
rules.passCriteria: Returns 405, any 2xx, 400, or 404 response
rules.failCriteria: Returns a response other than 405, 2xx, 400, or 404

rules.name: Rejects JSON-RPC batch requests
rules.description: Verifies the server rejects JSON-RPC batch (array) requests
rules.passCriteria: Returns 4xx HTTP status or JSON-RPC error for batch array (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After); any other 403 counts only when the same ping sent alone (a 429 on it retried once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429), whatever its message says; a 5xx counts only with the server's own -32600 (with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx)
rules.failCriteria: Processes batch request or returns no error; a 5xx without the server's own -32600 (a -32603, a server-defined code, or no JSON-RPC error); not evaluable when a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place, or its single-ping twin drew the same 403 (quoted when its message names Host/Origin validation), a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: Notification returns 202 Accepted
rules.description: Verifies the server returns exactly HTTP 202 Accepted for JSON-RPC notifications (MUST per spec)
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 202 Accepted response
rules.failCriteria: Any status code other than 202 (including 200, 204)

rules.name: Enforces MCP-Session-Id after init
rules.description: Verifies the server enforces MCP-Session-Id header after initialization
rules.passCriteria: Returns 400 for missing session ID, or auto-pass if no session ID was issued
rules.failCriteria: Returns 2xx without required session ID header

rules.name: Returns 404 for unknown session ID
rules.description: Sends request with fabricated MCP-Session-Id, verifies server returns 404
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 404 for unknown session ID
rules.failCriteria: Server accepts unknown session ID or returns wrong status code

rules.name: Initialize response has valid content type
rules.description: Validates that the initialize response uses application/json or text/event-stream content type
rules.passCriteria: Content-Type is application/json or text/event-stream
rules.failCriteria: Content-Type is neither application/json nor text/event-stream

rules.name: GET with session returns SSE or 405
rules.description: Tests the GET endpoint with an active session ID for server-initiated messages
rules.passCriteria: Returns text/event-stream or 405 Method Not Allowed
rules.failCriteria: Returns other status or content type

rules.name: Handles concurrent requests
rules.description: Sends multiple JSON-RPC requests in parallel and verifies correct responses
rules.passCriteria: All concurrent requests receive responses with correct matching IDs
rules.failCriteria: Any response has mismatched ID or non-2xx status

rules.name: SSE responses include event: message
rules.description: Checks that SSE responses include the required event: message field
rules.passCriteria: SSE response includes event: message, or server responds with JSON (not SSE)
rules.failCriteria: SSE response has data: fields but no event: message field

rules.name: Initialize handshake
rules.description: Verifies the server completes the initialize handshake
rules.passCriteria: Result contains protocolVersion field
rules.failCriteria: protocolVersion is missing from result

rules.name: Returns valid protocol version
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a valid protocol version string
rules.passCriteria: protocolVersion is in YYYY-MM-DD format
rules.failCriteria: protocolVersion is not in YYYY-MM-DD format

rules.name: Includes serverInfo
rules.description: Verifies the server includes serverInfo in the initialize response
rules.passCriteria: serverInfo object is present with a name field
rules.failCriteria: serverInfo or name is missing

rules.name: Returns capabilities object
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a capabilities object
rules.passCriteria: capabilities is present and is an object
rules.failCriteria: capabilities is missing or not an object

rules.name: Response is valid JSON-RPC 2.0
rules.description: Verifies the server returns valid JSON-RPC 2.0 responses
rules.passCriteria: Response has jsonrpc="2.0", id present, and result or error present; an error envelope counts only when it is the server's own (a 403 next to the same ping sent on its own as application/json, a 429 on it retried once, that was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429) is; so is the server's own -32600/-32601/-32602 on a 5xx, with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx)
rules.failCriteria: Missing jsonrpc, id, or both result and error fields; an initialize answered without a result by a 401/auth 403, a 429, a 5xx without the server's own refusal, or a 403 next to the same ping sent on its own as application/json that drew the same 403, a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer is not evaluable, whatever JSON-RPC error its body carries

rules.name: Responds to ping
rules.description: Verifies the server responds to ping requests
rules.passCriteria: Result is present in the response
rules.failCriteria: Error response or no result

rules.name: Instructions field is valid
rules.description: Verifies the instructions field, if present, is a valid string
rules.passCriteria: instructions is absent or is a string
rules.failCriteria: instructions is present but not a string

rules.name: Response ID matches request ID
rules.description: Verifies the server echoes back the correct request ID
rules.passCriteria: Response id === request id
rules.failCriteria: Response id does not match request id

rules.name: Supports string request IDs
rules.description: Sends request with string id and verifies server echoes it back correctly
rules.passCriteria: String id echoed back with correct value and type
rules.failCriteria: Server does not echo back string id correctly

rules.name: Handles unknown protocol version
rules.description: Sends initialize with future protocol version, verifies server negotiates down or errors
rules.passCriteria: Server returns its own supported version, or rejects with a JSON-RPC error next to a handshake that was served or drew a different status, a 403 without a Bearer challenge included whatever its message says (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After; a 5xx counts only with the server's own -32600/-32602, with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx); an HTTP connection closed without an answer counts only next to the served handshake
rules.failCriteria: Server blindly accepts impossible future version; an HTTP error status without a JSON-RPC error; a 5xx without the server's own -32600/-32602; not evaluable when the handshake was rejected the same way or a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place; a timeout, refused connection or stdio server already gone is server unreachable; a stdio server that exits on the probe (over stdio always a second initialize on the live session) died on a second initialize, not on the version (and is restarted for the tests after it); any other transport failure is no usable response

rules.name: Rejects second initialize request
rules.description: Sends second initialize in same session, verifies server rejects it
rules.passCriteria: Server returns a JSON-RPC error or 4xx for the duplicate initialize (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After); a 403 counts whatever its message names, since the handshake was served with the same Host and Origin; the server's own -32600 on a 5xx passes with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx; a closed connection counts only next to the served handshake
rules.failCriteria: Server accepts second initialize without error; a 3xx; a 5xx without the server's own -32600; not evaluable when the handshake was not served or a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place; a timeout or refused connection is server unreachable

rules.name: logging/setLevel accepted
rules.description: Verifies the server accepts logging/setLevel requests
rules.passCriteria: No error in response, or auto-pass if logging capability not advertised
rules.failCriteria: Error response when logging capability is advertised

rules.name: completion/complete accepted
rules.description: Verifies the server handles completion/complete requests
rules.passCriteria: Result returned or -32602 error, or auto-pass if completions capability not advertised
rules.failCriteria: Error other than -32602 when completions capability is advertised

rules.name: Handles cancellation notifications
rules.description: Verifies the server accepts notifications/cancelled without error
rules.passCriteria: Server accepts cancellation notification (2xx response)
rules.failCriteria: Server returns error for cancellation notification

rules.name: Handles progress notifications gracefully
rules.description: Sends notifications/progress to the server and verifies it handles it gracefully. Note: per spec, progress flows server-to-client; this tests resilience to unexpected notifications.
rules.passCriteria: Server accepts notification without error (2xx response)
rules.failCriteria: Server returns non-2xx for an unexpected notification

rules.name: Accepts listChanged notifications
rules.description: Sends listChanged notifications for declared capabilities and verifies server accepts them
rules.passCriteria: Server accepts all applicable listChanged notifications (2xx)
rules.failCriteria: Server rejects listChanged notification with non-2xx

rules.name: Supports progress tokens in requests
rules.description: Calls a tool (the first without required arguments, preferring one that mentions progress) with _meta.progressToken and judges every notifications/progress on the response
rules.passCriteria: Every notifications/progress carries the request's token with a strictly increasing numeric progress value (no notifications at all also passes); a served call, a 2xx with no JSON-RPC response, a 429/401/auth 403, or a server error the token is not shown to cause is an observation, not a skip; a tools/call that gets no answer measured nothing (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: A progress notification carrying a foreign token, without params, or with a non-numeric or non-increasing progress value; a server error (a JSON-RPC error, or an HTTP status >= 400 other than 429/401/auth 403) on the call carrying the token when the same call without it is served and the call carrying it, resent after that, draws a server error again

rules.name: tools/list returns valid response
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a valid tools/list response
rules.passCriteria: Returns a tools array
rules.failCriteria: Response does not contain a tools array

rules.name: tools/call responds correctly
rules.description: Verifies the server responds correctly to tools/call requests
rules.passCriteria: Returns content array or any JSON-RPC error
rules.failCriteria: Returns neither content array nor error

rules.name: tools/list supports pagination
rules.description: Verifies the server supports pagination for tools/list
rules.passCriteria: No nextCursor (single page) or valid string cursor with working next page
rules.failCriteria: Invalid cursor value or broken pagination

rules.name: Tool content items have valid types
rules.description: Verifies that tool call content items use valid type values
rules.passCriteria: All content item types are in [text, image, audio, resource, resource_link] or tool returns an error; an empty content array, or an error, leaves nothing to validate (a skip); content that is not an array, or no result, passes unflagged (tools-call fails it)
rules.failCriteria: Content item has an unknown type

rules.name: resources/list returns valid response
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a valid resources/list response
rules.passCriteria: Returns a resources array
rules.failCriteria: Response does not contain a resources array

rules.name: resources/read returns content
rules.description: Verifies the server returns valid content for resources/read
rules.passCriteria: Returns contents array with uri and text or blob fields
rules.failCriteria: Missing contents array, uri, or both text and blob

rules.name: resources/templates/list returns valid response
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a valid resource templates response
rules.passCriteria: Returns resourceTemplates array or -32601 (method not found) error
rules.failCriteria: Error other than -32601

rules.name: resources/list supports pagination
rules.description: Verifies the server supports pagination for resources/list
rules.passCriteria: No nextCursor (single page) or valid string cursor with working next page
rules.failCriteria: Invalid cursor value or broken pagination

rules.name: Resource subscribe/unsubscribe
rules.description: Verifies the server supports resource subscribe and unsubscribe
rules.passCriteria: Both subscribe and unsubscribe succeed
rules.failCriteria: Either subscribe or unsubscribe returns an error

rules.name: prompts/list returns valid response
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a valid prompts/list response
rules.passCriteria: Returns a prompts array
rules.failCriteria: Response does not contain a prompts array

rules.name: prompts/get returns valid messages
rules.description: Verifies the server returns valid messages for prompts/get
rules.passCriteria: Returns messages array with role and content fields, or error
rules.failCriteria: Invalid messages structure

rules.name: prompts/list supports pagination
rules.description: Verifies the server supports pagination for prompts/list
rules.passCriteria: No nextCursor (single page) or valid string cursor with working next page
rules.failCriteria: Invalid cursor value or broken pagination

rules.name: Returns JSON-RPC error for unknown method
rules.description: Verifies the server returns a JSON-RPC error for unknown methods
rules.passCriteria: Any JSON-RPC error response, next to a handshake that was served or drew a different status (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After; a 5xx counts only with the server's own -32601, with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx); any other 403 counts only when a ping with the same headers (a 429 on it retried once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429), whatever its message says
rules.failCriteria: No error returned for unknown method; a 5xx without the server's own -32601; not evaluable when the handshake was rejected the same way, a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place, or the ping drew the same 403 (quoted when its message names Host/Origin validation), a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: Uses correct JSON-RPC error code for unknown method
rules.description: Verifies the server uses the standard error code for unknown methods
rules.passCriteria: Error code === -32601 (Method not found)
rules.failCriteria: Error code is not -32601

rules.name: Handles malformed JSON-RPC
rules.description: Verifies the server handles malformed JSON-RPC requests
rules.passCriteria: JSON-RPC error response or HTTP 4xx status that is the server's own rejection (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After; any other 403 counts only when a well-formed ping with the same headers (a 429 on it retried once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429); the server's own -32600 on a 5xx passes with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx)
rules.failCriteria: Neither JSON-RPC error nor HTTP 4xx, or a 5xx without the server's own -32600; not evaluable when the handshake was rejected the same way, a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place whatever JSON-RPC error its body carries, or the ping drew the same 403 (quoted when its message names Host/Origin validation), a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: Handles invalid JSON body
rules.description: Verifies the server handles invalid JSON in the request body
rules.passCriteria: JSON-RPC error response or HTTP 4xx status that is the server's own rejection (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After; any other 403 counts only when a well-formed ping with the same headers (a 429 on it retried once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429); the server's own -32700 on a 5xx passes with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx)
rules.failCriteria: Neither JSON-RPC error nor HTTP 4xx, or a 5xx without the server's own -32700; not evaluable when the handshake was rejected the same way, a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place whatever JSON-RPC error its body carries, or the ping drew the same 403 (quoted when its message names Host/Origin validation), a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: Returns error for tools/call without name
rules.description: Verifies the server returns an error when tools/call is missing the name parameter
rules.passCriteria: The server's own JSON-RPC error, or isError flag in result (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After; any other 403 counts only when the same request for ping (a 429 on it retried once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx or a 4xx other than 401/403/429); the server's own -32602 on a 5xx passes with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx)
rules.failCriteria: No error returned, or a 5xx without the server's own -32602; not evaluable when the handshake was rejected the same way, a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place whatever JSON-RPC error its body carries, or the ping drew the same 403, a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: Returns -32700 for invalid JSON
rules.description: Verifies the server returns the standard parse error code for invalid JSON
rules.passCriteria: Error code === -32700 (Parse error)
rules.failCriteria: Error code is not -32700 or no error

rules.name: Returns -32600 for invalid request
rules.description: Verifies the server returns the standard error code for invalid requests
rules.passCriteria: Error code === -32600 (Invalid Request)
rules.failCriteria: Error code is not -32600 or no error

rules.name: Returns error for unknown tool name
rules.description: Verifies the server returns an error when calling an unknown tool
rules.passCriteria: JSON-RPC error or isError=true in result
rules.failCriteria: No error returned for unknown tool

rules.name: Rejects methods for undeclared capabilities
rules.description: Calls list methods for undeclared capabilities and verifies server returns errors
rules.passCriteria: Server returns its own error for methods of undeclared capabilities (a 429 is retried once after Retry-After; the server's own -32601 on a 5xx passes with a warning that a rejected request should get a 4xx); a server that declares all three capabilities has nothing to probe (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Server returns success for methods it did not declare capability for, or a 5xx without the server's own -32601; not evaluable when the initialize handshake was not served (no declaration was seen; each method's answer is listed), or when a 401/auth 403/repeated 429 answered in the server's place, or the same request for ping (asked once, a 429 on it retried once) drew the same 403, a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer

rules.name: Handles invalid pagination cursor gracefully
rules.description: Sends garbage pagination cursor to a list method
rules.passCriteria: Server returns error or ignores invalid cursor
rules.failCriteria: Server crashes or returns no error/result

rules.name: All tools have name and inputSchema
rules.description: Verifies all tools have a valid name and inputSchema
rules.passCriteria: All tools have valid name (1-128 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+) and inputSchema object with type "object"; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Any tool has invalid name or missing/invalid inputSchema

rules.name: Tool annotations are valid
rules.description: Verifies tool annotations have correct types
rules.passCriteria: Hint fields are booleans, title field is a string; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Type mismatch in annotation fields

rules.name: Tools include title field
rules.description: Verifies the tool title field, if present, is valid
rules.passCriteria: title is absent or is a valid string; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: title is present but not a string

rules.name: Tools with outputSchema are valid
rules.description: Verifies tools with outputSchema have a valid JSON Schema object
rules.passCriteria: outputSchema is absent or is a valid JSON Schema object; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: outputSchema is present but not a valid JSON Schema object

rules.name: Prompts have name field
rules.description: Verifies all prompts have a name field and valid arguments
rules.passCriteria: All prompts have a name field and valid arguments if present; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Any prompt is missing name or has invalid arguments

rules.name: Resources have uri and name
rules.description: Verifies all resources have a valid parseable URI and name
rules.passCriteria: All resources have a valid parseable URI and name field; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Any resource is missing uri, has an invalid URI, or is missing name

rules.name: Rejects unauthenticated requests
rules.description: Verifies the server rejects requests without an Authorization header
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 401, or a 403 with a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge, for the unauthenticated request (without --auth, a 401 on the unauthenticated initialize counts when the preflight was neither served nor an auth refusal); with --auth a bare 403 or dropped connection also passes when the same ping with the credential is served (a 429 on it retried once)
rules.failCriteria: Server serves an unauthenticated request (initialize served with no credential fails as not requiring auth whatever the preflight answered); any other status that is not 401/403 fails worded for what it was (4xx/5xx/3xx/unserved 2xx), not as accepted; a bare 403 that cannot be attributed to authentication is not evaluable (allow the hostname you tested through when the message names Host/Origin validation); a timeout, refused connection or unattributable drop is server unreachable

rules.name: 401 responses include WWW-Authenticate header
rules.description: Checks that 401 responses include WWW-Authenticate header per RFC 9110
rules.passCriteria: 401 response includes WWW-Authenticate header; a 403 with a Bearer challenge is read the same way (the details name HTTP 403), and a bare 403 passes as not applicable (a skip); any other answer, or a closed connection counted as the rejection, leaves no challenge to check (a skip); skipped without --auth, and skipped as not evaluable when security-auth-required found a bare 403 it could not attribute to authentication (also when security-auth-required is filtered out); a probe with no HTTP answer fails as server unreachable (a timeout or a connection never established always, a closed connection unless the same request with the credential was served)
rules.failCriteria: 401 response missing WWW-Authenticate header

rules.name: Rejects malformed auth credentials
rules.description: Verifies the server rejects malformed Authorization header values
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 401 or 403 for garbage auth token; skipped without --auth, and skipped as not evaluable when security-auth-required found a bare 403 it could not attribute to authentication (also when security-auth-required is filtered out); a probe with no HTTP answer fails as server unreachable (a timeout or a connection never established always, a closed connection unless the same request with the credential was served); a pass is skipped when the configured credential itself draws 401 on the credentialed ping
rules.failCriteria: Server serves the malformed auth token; another status that is not 401/403 fails worded for what it was

rules.name: Enforces HTTPS/TLS
rules.description: Verifies the server rejects plaintext HTTP connections when HTTPS is configured
rules.passCriteria: HTTP connection rejected, redirected, or server URL uses HTTP (skipped)
rules.failCriteria: Server accepts plaintext HTTP alongside HTTPS

rules.name: Session IDs are high-entropy
rules.description: Verifies MCP-Session-Id values are cryptographically random
rules.passCriteria: Session ID is ≥16 chars, non-sequential, with high character diversity
rules.failCriteria: Session ID is short, purely numeric, or low-entropy

rules.name: Session ID does not bypass auth
rules.description: Verifies that a valid session ID alone is not sufficient for authentication
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 401 or 403 when session ID is sent without Authorization header; skipped without --auth or without a session ID, and skipped as not evaluable when security-auth-required found a bare 403 it could not attribute to authentication (also when security-auth-required is filtered out); a probe with no HTTP answer fails as server unreachable (a timeout or a connection never established always, a closed connection unless the same request with the credential was served)
rules.failCriteria: Server serves a request with session ID but no auth; another status that is not 401/403 fails worded for what it was

rules.name: Protected Resource Metadata endpoint exists
rules.description: Verifies Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) is published where clients look for it: the WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL when the unauthenticated ping's challenge carries one, else /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource followed by the endpoint path, then /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Falls back to legacy /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server with a warning.
rules.passCriteria: The WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL (only it), or without one the first well-known location with a valid document, returns JSON with resource and a non-empty authorization_servers array (a resource that is not the endpoint passes with a warning), or, with no document at any well-known location, legacy OAuth AS metadata exists (with a warning); skipped without --auth; skipped as not evaluable when every well-known location and the legacy document drew the same bare 403 security-auth-required could not attribute to authentication
rules.failCriteria: A challenge resource_metadata that is not an absolute http(s) URL, or is unreachable, non-200 or malformed; no well-known location answers; a malformed document and no valid one; no PRM and no legacy OAuth AS metadata; an unauthenticated ping with no HTTP answer is server unreachable (except a connection closed next to the served credentialed handshake)

rules.name: Rejects auth tokens in query string
rules.description: Verifies the server does not accept auth tokens in the URL query string
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 401 or 403 when token is in query string instead of Authorization header; skipped without --auth, and a 2xx fails whatever else is true; a 401/403 is skipped as not evaluable when security-auth-required found a bare 403 it could not attribute to authentication (the probe is still sent); a refusal is skipped when the configured credential itself draws 401 on the credentialed ping (also when security-auth-required is filtered out); a probe with no HTTP answer fails as server unreachable (a timeout or a connection never established always, a closed connection unless the same request with the credential was served)
rules.failCriteria: Server accepts token from query string

rules.name: CORS headers are restrictive
rules.description: Verifies CORS headers on an OPTIONS preflight and on a ping POST carrying a foreign Origin do not allow a wildcard or reflected origin
rules.passCriteria: No CORS headers on either answer, or Access-Control-Allow-Origin is not '*' or reflected; when neither probe gets an HTTP answer, connections closed on both pass as cross-origin refused only next to the served initialize handshake
rules.failCriteria: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*' or reflects arbitrary origins on either answer; when neither probe gets an HTTP answer (a timeout, a refused connection, any other failure, or connections closed when the handshake was not served) it is server unreachable

rules.name: Validates Origin header on requests
rules.description: Sends request with suspicious Origin header, verifies server validates it for DNS rebinding protection
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 403 or another 4xx refusing the untrusted Origin; a 401/403 only when initialize (the same headers without the Origin) was served or drew a different status, otherwise the check skips as not attributable to the Origin (see security-auth-required); one 429 is retried after Retry-After; a closed connection only when initialize was served
rules.failCriteria: Server accepts the request (2xx); a 5xx (the server failing, not refusing); a 429 that survives one retry (not evaluable); a redirect; no HTTP answer (server unreachable)

rules.name: Resists command injection in tool params
rules.description: Verifies tools do not execute OS command injection payloads in string parameters
rules.passCriteria: Injection payloads do not produce command execution output (output that only reflects the payload back is benign); unanswered payloads (timeouts, drops the server outlives) are counted apart, and none answered passes as inconclusive with a warning (recorded as a skip); with no listed tool that has a string parameter it is skipped
rules.failCriteria: Tool output contains evidence of command execution, or the server dies on a payload (stdio exit, restarted for the checks that follow; HTTP drop with no follow-up ping answer); a server already gone before a payload is server unreachable

rules.name: Resists SQL injection in tool params
rules.description: Verifies tools do not expose SQL injection vulnerabilities
rules.passCriteria: Injection payloads do not trigger database errors or data leakage (output that only reflects the payload back is benign); unanswered payloads (timeouts, drops the server outlives) are counted apart, and none answered passes as inconclusive with a warning (recorded as a skip); with no listed tool that has a string parameter it is skipped
rules.failCriteria: Tool output contains SQL error messages or database metadata, or the server dies on a payload (stdio exit, restarted for the checks that follow; HTTP drop with no follow-up ping answer); a server already gone before a payload is server unreachable

rules.name: Resists path traversal in tool params
rules.description: Verifies tools do not allow path traversal attacks via string parameters
rules.passCriteria: Traversal payloads do not return sensitive file content (output that only reflects the payload back is benign); unanswered payloads (timeouts, drops the server outlives) are counted apart, and none answered passes as inconclusive with a warning (recorded as a skip); with no listed tool that has a string parameter it is skipped
rules.failCriteria: Tool output contains content from /etc/passwd or system files, or the server dies on a payload (stdio exit, restarted for the checks that follow; HTTP drop with no follow-up ping answer); a server already gone before a payload is server unreachable

rules.name: Resists SSRF to internal networks
rules.description: Verifies tools with URL parameters do not fetch internal/cloud metadata endpoints
rules.passCriteria: Internal IP payloads do not return cloud metadata or internal service data (output that only reflects the payload back is benign); unanswered payloads (timeouts, drops the server outlives) are counted apart, and none answered passes as inconclusive with a warning (recorded as a skip); with no listed tool that has a URL-named string parameter it is skipped
rules.failCriteria: Tool output contains cloud metadata or internal network responses, or the server dies on a payload (stdio exit, restarted for the checks that follow; HTTP drop with no follow-up ping answer); a server already gone before a payload is server unreachable

rules.name: Handles oversized inputs gracefully
rules.description: Verifies the server handles a 1 MiB string in a tools/call, sent through the transport on HTTP and stdio, without crashing
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 413 or another 4xx that is not a gate's 401/403/429, a JSON-RPC error (rejected) or result (survived, with a body-limit warning), or a dropped connection the server outlives (follow-up ping served, answered by its id below HTTP 500, or refused with 401/403)
rules.failCriteria: 5xx, no JSON-RPC result or error, a gate's 429/401/403 (not evaluable), timeout, a crash (dropped connection with no follow-up answer, or a stdio exit), a run where nothing was answered, a refused connection, or an unparseable response

rules.name: Rejects or ignores extra tool params
rules.description: Verifies the server handles unexpected additional tool parameters safely
rules.passCriteria: Server rejects extra params with a JSON-RPC error or silently ignores them (a result); a timeout, or a dropped HTTP connection the server outlives, passes as inconclusive with a warning (recorded as a skip)
rules.failCriteria: HTTP 5xx; an answer with no result or error; a crash (a stdio child that exits on the call -- restarted for the tests that follow -- or a dropped HTTP connection after which the follow-up ping is not answered); a server already gone before the call (server unreachable); no usable response

rules.name: All tools define inputSchema
rules.description: Verifies all tools have an inputSchema with type 'object' for input validation
rules.passCriteria: All tools have inputSchema with type: 'object'; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Any tool is missing inputSchema or has wrong type

rules.name: Tool definitions are stable across calls
rules.description: Verifies tool definitions do not change between consecutive tools/list calls
rules.passCriteria: Tool count, names, and descriptions are identical across 2 calls; after a stdio restart that followed tools-list, both lists come from the new process (one read at the restart before any tools/call, one after a tools/call with no arguments), and the test skips with a warning when the new process leaves nothing to compare
rules.failCriteria: Tool definitions changed between calls (possible rug-pull attack)

rules.name: Tool descriptions free of injection patterns
rules.description: Scans tool descriptions for prompt injection patterns and hidden characters
rules.passCriteria: No suspicious patterns found in tool names, descriptions, or parameter descriptions; an empty list leaves nothing to validate (a skip)
rules.failCriteria: Tool descriptions contain 'ignore previous', 'override', hidden Unicode, or Base64 payloads

rules.name: Tools do not reference other tools by name
rules.description: Checks that tool descriptions do not reference other tool names
rules.passCriteria: No tool description contains the name of another tool
rules.failCriteria: Tool description references another tool by name (manipulation risk)

rules.name: Error responses do not leak stack traces
rules.description: Verifies error responses do not contain stack traces, file paths, or sensitive data
rules.passCriteria: No stack traces, file paths, connection strings, or credentials in error responses; skipped over stdio (raw HTTP probes); over HTTP a probe nothing answers fails as server unreachable
rules.failCriteria: Error response contains implementation details or sensitive information

rules.name: Error responses do not leak internal IPs
rules.description: Verifies error responses do not contain private IP addresses
rules.passCriteria: No 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, or 127.x addresses in error responses; skipped over stdio (raw HTTP probes); over HTTP a probe nothing answers fails as server unreachable
rules.failCriteria: Error response contains internal IP addresses

rules.name: Rate limiting is enforced
rules.description: Verifies the server implements rate limiting under burst load
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 429 returned during 50-request burst
rules.failCriteria: No 429 in the burst; more than half 5xx; every ping refused 401/403 before reaching a handler (not evaluable, naming the auth gate, or pointing at security-auth-required for a 403 that is no auth refusal); no ping answered (server unreachable)

rules.name: Newline-delimited JSON framing
rules.description: Verifies a stdio server emits each JSON-RPC response as a single line on stdout, terminated by \n, under rapid-fire requests
rules.passCriteria: Every response is exactly one newline-terminated line of parseable JSON
rules.failCriteria: Any response is split across lines, merged with another response, or missing a trailing newline

rules.name: UTF-8 unicode roundtrip
rules.description: Sends non-ASCII (Latin-1, CJK + emoji) parameters to a stdio server and verifies they survive the round trip
rules.passCriteria: The chosen tool (one named echo, else the first with a string property named message/text/input/query, else the first tool; tools/list read on demand) reproduces the probe byte-for-byte or piece by piece; or, when the tool does not echo or there is no tool to call, a ping whose _meta carries the probe is answered with a result
rules.failCriteria: The tool reply or the ping reply shows mangling (U+FFFD, a Latin-1 mis-decode, '?' substitution, or the non-ASCII characters dropped), the tool call draws -32700, the ping is rejected or answered with a non-JSON-RPC reply, or a probe gets no reply, or is answered by a child that then exits or stops answering (a plain ping between the probes, and a wait of up to 250 ms plus a plain ping after the last one, each ping with the per-request timeout, find it gone; a child silent for the whole --timeout fails as a hang, named in a warning and not restarted) (a child that exited is restarted; one already gone is server unreachable)

rules.name: Recovers after unknown method
rules.description: Sends an unknown method followed by a valid ping; verifies the server errors on the unknown method but keeps serving subsequent requests
rules.passCriteria: Unknown method receives a JSON-RPC error and the follow-up ping succeeds
rules.failCriteria: Server exits, closes stdout, or fails to respond to the follow-up ping

rules.name: Sampling capability shape
rules.description: Verifies the server's initialize response does NOT declare sampling as its own capability (sampling is a client capability)
rules.passCriteria: Server capabilities object does not contain a 'sampling' key
rules.failCriteria: Server declares 'sampling' in its own capabilities

rules.name: Roots capability shape
rules.description: Verifies the server's initialize response does NOT declare roots as its own capability (roots is a client capability)
rules.passCriteria: Server capabilities object does not contain a 'roots' key
rules.failCriteria: Server declares 'roots' in its own capabilities

rules.name: Elicitation capability shape
rules.description: Verifies the server's initialize response does NOT declare elicitation as its own capability (elicitation is a client capability added in 2025-11-25)
rules.passCriteria: Server capabilities object does not contain an 'elicitation' key
rules.failCriteria: Server declares 'elicitation' in its own capabilities

rules.name: Tolerates _meta field on requests
rules.description: Sends a ping with params._meta = { extra: 'value' } and verifies the server does not reject the request. The 2025-11-25 spec reserves _meta for forward-compat extension metadata on any request
rules.passCriteria: Server returns a normal result regardless of unknown _meta keys
rules.failCriteria: Server returns a JSON-RPC error that cites the _meta field

rules.name: HTTP POST accepted
rules.description: POSTs a conformant server/discover request (standard headers plus _meta) to the MCP endpoint and verifies a 2xx status. The server MUST provide a single endpoint that supports POST and every client message MUST be its own POST; this is the baseline every other HTTP test builds on.
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 2xx for a POST carrying a conformant server/discover request (standard headers plus _meta).
rules.failCriteria: Any non-2xx status; a 401/403 is annotated as authentication required (no --auth, and a 401 or a 403 carrying a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge), as the configured credential rejected (--auth given, and a 401 or a 403 whose Bearer challenge carries an error parameter), or as forbidden (any other 403, which may be Host/Origin validation, a gateway, missing credentials or the token's permissions).

rules.name: Responds with JSON or SSE
rules.description: Checks the Content-Type of the server/discover response. For a JSON-RPC request the server MUST return either application/json (a single object) or text/event-stream (a request-scoped SSE stream); nothing else is valid.
rules.passCriteria: The Content-Type of the server/discover response contains application/json or text/event-stream.
rules.failCriteria: Any other Content-Type, or none.

rules.name: Rejects non-JSON request Content-Type
rules.description: Sends an otherwise valid server/discover (correct headers and _meta) with Content-Type: text/plain and expects a 4xx status. The POST body MUST be a single JSON-RPC message; a server that parses text/plain as JSON is trusting a content type it never checked. A rejection is credited only when it is the server's own: a 429 is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s), and a 401, a 403 that reads as an auth refusal (an auth gate: without --auth any Bearer challenge, with --auth one carrying an error parameter; a gateway's -32001 body included), a 429 still a 429 after the resend, or any other 403 that a conformant server/discover sent next to it could not get past either fails as not evaluable. That twin is sent through the suite's client (the same credential and protocol headers) only for such a 403, is resent once on a 429, and credits the 403 only when it was served or drew a status the server itself chose (a 2xx, or a 4xx other than 401, 403 or 429); when it drew the same 403, a message naming Host/Origin validation is quoted. Any rejection -- a status >= 400, or a JSON-RPC error on a 2xx -- also fails as not evaluable when the conformant setup server/discover was itself rejected or got no response: a server that rejects everything proves nothing by rejecting text/plain too. When that setup server/discover already drew the probe's 403, its answer is the twin and no further server/discover is sent. Otherwise any 5xx fails as the server failing on the request rather than rejecting it (a broken server, or a gateway with no backend). A probe that gets no answer, or whose resend after a 429 gets none, fails as server unreachable.
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 4xx (415 or 400 expected) for an otherwise valid server/discover sent with Content-Type: text/plain, as the server's own rejection, with the conformant setup server/discover served. A 429 is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s), and any 403 that is not an auth refusal (one without a Bearer challenge, or with --auth one whose challenge carries no error parameter) is read as the server's only when a conformant server/discover sent next to it (a 429 on it resent once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx, or a 4xx other than 401, 403 or 429).
rules.failCriteria: The text/plain body is parsed and answered with a 2xx status, or a redirect; or the POST gets no answer, the resend after a 429 included ("server unreachable"). A rejecting status fails as not evaluable when it is a 401, a 403 that reads as an auth refusal (without --auth any Bearer challenge, with --auth one carrying an error parameter; a gateway's -32001 body included), a 429 still a 429 after its one resend, or any other 403 the conformant server/discover could not get past either (it drew the same 403, a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer), and any rejection (a status >= 400, or a JSON-RPC error on a 2xx) does when the conformant setup server/discover was itself rejected or got no response (when that discover drew the probe's 403, its answer is the twin and no further server/discover is sent). Otherwise any 5xx fails as the server failing on the POST rather than rejecting it (a broken server, or a gateway with no backend).

rules.name: Rejects JSON-RPC batch requests
rules.description: POSTs a JSON array containing two valid server/discover requests and expects a 4xx status or a JSON-RPC error. The POST body MUST be a single JSON-RPC request or notification; batches were dropped in 2025-06-18 and remain unsupported. On a text/event-stream answer only JSON-RPC responses count: notifications before the error are ignored, and a stream that carries no response fails. An SSE data frame holding an array is the processed-batch shape, as the same array over application/json is, whatever its elements say. A rejection is credited only when it is the server's own: a 429 is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s), and a 401, a 403 that reads as an auth refusal (an auth gate: without --auth any Bearer challenge, with --auth one carrying an error parameter; a gateway's -32001 body included), a 429 still a 429 after the resend, or any other 403 that a conformant server/discover sent next to it could not get past either fails as not evaluable. That twin is sent through the suite's client (the same credential and protocol headers) only for such a 403, is resent once on a 429, and credits the 403 only when it was served or drew a status the server itself chose (a 2xx, or a 4xx other than 401, 403 or 429); when it drew the same 403, a message naming Host/Origin validation is quoted. Any rejection -- a status >= 400, or a JSON-RPC error on any status (a gateway's -32001 on HTTP 200 included) -- also fails as not evaluable when the conformant setup server/discover was itself rejected or got no response, as the standard-header rules do: a legacy-only server pinned to this catalog, or a proxy answering every POST 404, proves nothing by rejecting the batch too, and a -32600 on a 5xx is then neither credited nor warned about. When that setup server/discover already drew the probe's 403, its answer is the twin and no further server/discover is sent. Otherwise a 5xx without -32600 fails as the server failing on the batch rather than rejecting it (a broken server, or a gateway with no backend), and a -32600 on a 5xx is credited, with a warning that a 4xx is expected. A probe that gets no answer, or whose resend after a 429 gets none, fails as server unreachable.
rules.passCriteria: A JSON array of two valid server/discover requests draws HTTP 4xx or a JSON-RPC error body, as the server's own rejection, with the conformant setup server/discover served. A 429 is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s), a -32600 on a 5xx passes with a warning that a 4xx is expected, and any 403 that is not an auth refusal (one without a Bearer challenge, or with --auth one whose challenge carries no error parameter) is read as the server's only when a conformant server/discover sent next to it (a 429 on it resent once) was served or drew a status the server chose (a 2xx, or a 4xx other than 401, 403 or 429).
rules.failCriteria: A 2xx status without a JSON-RPC error, an array response (a JSON array body, or an SSE data frame holding an array), or a text/event-stream carrying no JSON-RPC response (notifications before an error frame are ignored); or the batch gets no answer, the resend after a 429 included ("server unreachable"). A rejecting status fails as not evaluable when it is a 401, a 403 that reads as an auth refusal (without --auth any Bearer challenge, with --auth one carrying an error parameter; a gateway's -32001 body included), a 429 still a 429 after its one resend, or any other 403 the conformant server/discover could not get past either (it drew the same 403, a 401, a 429 again, a 5xx, a redirect or no answer), and any rejection (a status >= 400, or a JSON-RPC error on any status) does when the conformant setup server/discover was itself rejected or got no response (a -32600 on a 5xx is then neither credited nor warned about; when that discover drew the probe's 403, its answer is the twin and no further server/discover is sent). Otherwise a 5xx without -32600 fails as the server failing on the batch rather than rejecting it (a broken server, or a gateway with no backend).

rules.name: Notification returns 202 Accepted
rules.description: POSTs a notifications/cancelled notification (no id) for an unknown request and expects HTTP 202 Accepted with an empty body. If the server accepts a notification it MUST return exactly 202; if it cannot accept it, it MUST return an HTTP error status. 202 passes, a 4xx refusal passes with a warning (this revision defines no client notifications over HTTP), and 200, 204 or 5xx fail.
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 202 for a POSTed notifications/cancelled; a 4xx refusal also passes but is reported as a warning.
rules.failCriteria: HTTP 200, 204, or any 5xx.

rules.name: Handles concurrent requests
rules.description: Fires three server/discover requests in parallel over separate POSTs and verifies every response arrives with its own matching id. Each message is its own HTTP POST with no shared session, so a stateless server must serve overlapping requests without cross-talk.
rules.passCriteria: Three parallel server/discover POSTs each return a 2xx response whose id matches the request that produced it.
rules.failCriteria: Any response missing, non-2xx, or carrying the id of a different request.

rules.name: GET returns 405
rules.description: Sends HTTP GET to the MCP endpoint. The standalone GET SSE stream was removed in 2026-07-28 (subscriptions/listen replaces it) and a server on this revision SHOULD answer legacy GET traffic with 405 Method Not Allowed. 405 passes, another 4xx passes with a warning, and a text/event-stream response fails.
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 405 for GET on the MCP endpoint; another 4xx passes with a warning.
rules.failCriteria: A text/event-stream response, any 2xx, or any 5xx.

rules.name: DELETE returns 405
rules.description: Sends HTTP DELETE to the MCP endpoint. Sessions and their DELETE termination were removed in 2026-07-28, so a server on this revision SHOULD answer with 405 Method Not Allowed. 405 passes, another 4xx passes with a warning, and 2xx or 5xx fail.
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 405 for DELETE on the MCP endpoint; another 4xx passes with a warning.
rules.failCriteria: Any 2xx or 5xx status.

rules.name: Ignores Mcp-Session-Id
rules.description: Sends a valid server/discover carrying a fabricated Mcp-Session-Id header and expects a normal result with no Mcp-Session-Id on the response. Protocol-level sessions are gone: a server SHOULD ignore the header and never mint or echo session ids. A 404 or 400 keyed to the bogus session, or a minted id, fails.
rules.passCriteria: A valid server/discover carrying a fabricated Mcp-Session-Id header returns a normal result with no Mcp-Session-Id header on the response.
rules.failCriteria: HTTP 404 or 400 keyed to the unknown session, or a minted or echoed Mcp-Session-Id response header.

rules.name: Rejects missing MCP-Protocol-Version header
rules.description: Sends a server/discover whose body is complete but whose MCP-Protocol-Version header is omitted. Every POST MUST carry the header, and a server that does not serve pre-2025-06-18 clients MUST reject its absence with HTTP 400 and a -32020 HeaderMismatch error. 400 is the hard requirement; a missing or different error code is reported as a warning. A 400 is credited only when the conformant server/discover was served; a server that rejects everything fails this test as not evaluable, as does a transport-level answer (401, 403, 413, 415 or 429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter).
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 400 for a complete server/discover body sent without the MCP-Protocol-Version header, credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (a server that rejects everything, or a 401/403/413/415/429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter, fails as not evaluable); a body without error code -32020 is reported as a warning.
rules.failCriteria: Any status other than 400, or a 400 or transport-level status (401, 403, 413, 415, 429) from a server whose conformant server/discover was itself rejected or unanswered.

rules.name: Rejects header/_meta version mismatch
rules.description: Sends MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28 with _meta protocolVersion 1999-01-01. The header value MUST match the _meta field, and on a mismatch the server MUST respond 400 Bad Request with a -32020 HeaderMismatch error; both the status and the code are checked here. The 400 is credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (401, 403, 413, 415 or 429).
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 400 and a JSON-RPC error with code -32020 when the header says 2026-07-28 and _meta says 1999-01-01, credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (a server that rejects everything, or a 401/403/413/415/429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter, fails as not evaluable).
rules.failCriteria: A status other than 400, an error code other than -32020, a result, or a 400 from a server whose conformant server/discover was itself rejected.

rules.name: Rejects missing Mcp-Method header
rules.description: Sends a valid server/discover body without the Mcp-Method header. Mcp-Method is REQUIRED on every request; a missing standard header is a validation failure and the server MUST answer HTTP 400 with a -32020 HeaderMismatch error. 400 is the hard requirement; the -32020 code is checked as a warning because an intermediary may reject with a bare 400. A 400 is credited only when the conformant server/discover was served; a server that rejects everything fails this test as not evaluable, as does a transport-level answer (401, 403, 413, 415 or 429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter).
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 400 for a valid server/discover body sent without the Mcp-Method header, credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (a server that rejects everything, or a 401/403/413/415/429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter, fails as not evaluable); a missing or different error code is reported as a warning.
rules.failCriteria: Any status other than 400, or a 400 from a server whose conformant server/discover was itself rejected or unanswered.

rules.name: Rejects Mcp-Method/body mismatch
rules.description: Sends a server/discover body with Mcp-Method: tools/list. A header that does not match the corresponding body value MUST be rejected with HTTP 400 and a -32020 HeaderMismatch error, because a gateway routing on the header and a server executing on the body would otherwise disagree. 400 is required; -32020 is a warning. A 400 is credited only when the conformant server/discover was served; a server that rejects everything fails this test as not evaluable, as does a transport-level answer (401, 403, 413, 415 or 429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter).
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 400 when Mcp-Method: tools/list is sent on a server/discover body, credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (a server that rejects everything, or a 401/403/413/415/429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter, fails as not evaluable); a missing -32020 code is reported as a warning.
rules.failCriteria: Any status other than 400 (the request was routed on one value and executed on another), or a 400 from a server whose conformant server/discover was itself rejected.

rules.name: Rejects Mcp-Name/body mismatch
rules.description: Sends a resources/read of the first listed resource (else a prompts/get of the first prompt without required arguments) whose Mcp-Name header names a different resource or prompt than the body. Mcp-Name is REQUIRED on tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get and MUST match params.uri or params.name after Base64 sentinel decoding, so the server MUST answer 400 + -32020; the 400 is credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (401, 403, 413, 415 or 429). The resource and prompt lists are fetched on demand when the feature tests did not run; skipped when the server declares neither capability or nothing listed can be read by name alone; when a declared list call failed (even if the other list worked but listed nothing readable by name) it skips pointing at the failed -list tests if they are in the run, and fails with the recorded reasons when they are not.
rules.passCriteria: HTTP 400 for a resources/read of the first listed resource (else a prompts/get of the first prompt without required arguments) whose Mcp-Name header names a different object than the body, credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (a server that rejects everything, or a 401/403/413/415/429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter, fails as not evaluable); a missing -32020 code is reported as a warning. The lists are fetched on demand; skipped when the server declares neither resources nor prompts or nothing listed is readable by name alone, and skipped pointing at the failed -list rules when a declared list call failed (even if the other list worked but held nothing readable by name) and those rules are in the run.
rules.failCriteria: Any status other than 400, a 400 from a server whose conformant server/discover was itself rejected, or a declared list call failed while its -list rule was filtered out of the run (the recorded reasons are named).

rules.name: Header names are case-insensitive
rules.description: Sends a valid server/discover with the standard headers spelled in lowercase (mcp-protocol-version, mcp-method) and expects a normal result. Header names are case-insensitive per RFC 9110 and servers MUST compare them that way; only values are case-sensitive. A 400 HeaderMismatch here means the server matches on exact spelling.
rules.passCriteria: A valid server/discover whose standard headers are spelled in lowercase (mcp-protocol-version, mcp-method) returns a normal result.
rules.failCriteria: HTTP 400 or any other rejection attributable to header spelling.

rules.name: No server-initiated requests on any stream
rules.description: Post-hoc scan of every message the server sent during the run (JSON bodies, SSE frames, stdio lines) for a frame carrying both method and id, i.e. a server-to-client JSON-RPC request. No such direction exists in 2026-07-28: sampling, elicitation and roots MUST travel inside an InputRequiredResult (MRTR), and the server MUST NOT send independent requests on a response stream or to stdout.
rules.passCriteria: No recorded server message on any response stream or on stdout carries both method and id.
rules.failCriteria: At least one server-to-client JSON-RPC request was observed during the run. Also fails when no server message was received during the run (an unreachable server): the scan then has nothing to attest.

rules.name: Newline-delimited JSON framing
rules.description: Writes five server/discover requests to stdin in rapid succession and expects five responses, each a single line of JSON terminated by a newline. Messages are newline-delimited and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines, and the server MUST NOT write anything to stdout that is not a valid MCP message.
rules.passCriteria: Five rapid server/discover requests each receive a response on its own newline-terminated line of JSON.
rules.failCriteria: Any of the five is unanswered, split across lines, or interleaved with non-JSON output on stdout.

rules.name: UTF-8 unicode roundtrip
rules.description: Calls a tool with CJK and emoji characters in its string arguments -- a tool named echo, else the first tool with a string property named message, text, input or query, else the first tool (tools/list is fetched on demand) -- and passes when the reply reproduces them byte-for-byte, or reproduces every non-ASCII piece of the probe somewhere in the reply (a tool that tokenizes its input). Fails on evidence of mangling: U+FFFD replacement characters, a Latin-1 mis-decode, the non-ASCII characters replaced by '?', the non-ASCII characters stripped (the probe's Latin-1 word or its ASCII skeleton present with neither the CJK word nor the emoji anywhere in the reply), or a -32700 parse error. A tool that merely does not echo its input proves nothing, so the verdict then rests on a server/discover whose clientInfo name carries the same characters: the server parsing and answering it is the round-trip verified, and rejecting or mangling it fails. The server crashing on, or never answering, whichever probe is sent fails too, with a one-line reason: a tool call that gets no reply ends the check there, without falling back to the discover. So does a child that answers a probe and then exits or stops answering: a plain server/discover is sent between the tool call and the envelope probe, and after the last answered probe the check waits up to 250 ms for the child to exit and, when it has not, sends a plain server/discover. Each of those requests gets the per-request timeout, so a server that answers within --timeout is never read as hung. A child that exits before --timeout runs out fails the check ('... was answered, but the server exited right after'), and so does one found gone when the next probe is about to be sent (the probe it answered last is charged). A child still running but silent for the whole --timeout fails as a hang ('... stopped answering right after'); a warning names the probe, and the child is not restarted. A child that exits on the probe, or right after answering it, is restarted (a fresh server/discover plus one request that pins its era) with a warning naming this check, on every attempt that kills it, --retries included, so the checks after it measure a live process; a child already gone before the probe was sent fails as server unreachable and is not restarted. Details keep to 220 characters: the note on what the tool call drew gives way first, then the tool's name in the request, never the conclusion. JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded on every transport; this catches latin-1 or platform-default decoding of stdin.
rules.passCriteria: The chosen tool (one named echo, else the first with a string property named message/text/input/query, else the first tool; tools/list fetched on demand) reproduces the CJK/emoji probe byte-for-byte, or reproduces every non-ASCII piece of it somewhere in the reply (a tokenizing tool); or, when the tool merely does not echo its input, a server/discover whose clientInfo name carries the probe is answered with a result.
rules.failCriteria: The tool reply or the discover reply shows mangling (U+FFFD, a Latin-1 mis-decode, the non-ASCII characters replaced by '?', or the probe's first word present with neither the CJK word nor the emoji anywhere in the reply), the tool call draws -32700, the discover carrying the probe in clientInfo is rejected or answered with a non-JSON-RPC reply, or a probe that is sent gets no reply because the server crashes or never answers it -- a tool call that gets none ends the check at once, without falling back to the discover (the details give a one-line reason, such as the exit code or the timeout) -- or a probe is answered by a child that then exits or stops answering (a plain server/discover between the tool call and the envelope probe, and after the last answered probe a wait of up to 250 ms for the exit followed by a plain server/discover, each with the per-request timeout, find it gone or get no reply; a child found gone when the next probe is about to be sent charges the probe it answered last; a child still running but silent for the whole --timeout fails as a hang, is named in a warning and is not restarted). Details keep to 220 characters, the note on the tool call and then the tool's name giving way, never the conclusion. A child that exits on the probe, or right after answering it, is restarted for the checks after this one, with a warning naming it, on every attempt; a child already gone before the probe was sent fails as server unreachable and is not restarted.

rules.name: Recovers after unknown method
rules.description: Sends a bogus method with a full modern _meta, then a valid server/discover immediately after. The unknown method should draw a JSON-RPC error (-32601 expected) and the server must keep serving: the discover that follows must succeed on the same process.
rules.passCriteria: The bogus method draws a JSON-RPC error (-32601 expected) and the server/discover sent immediately after succeeds on the same process.
rules.failCriteria: The process exits, stops answering, or the follow-up server/discover fails.

rules.name: Ignores cancellation of unknown request
rules.description: Writes a notifications/cancelled referencing a request id that was never issued, then a server/discover. On stdio notifications/cancelled is the only cancellation signal and servers MAY ignore one for an unknown or completed request; the discover that follows must still be answered and nothing may be emitted in reply to the notification.
rules.passCriteria: A notifications/cancelled for an unknown requestId produces no reply and the server/discover sent after it is answered normally.
rules.failCriteria: Any message emitted in reply to the notification, the follow-up server/discover is unanswered, or the process exits.

rules.name: server/discover returns DiscoverResult
rules.description: Sends server/discover with a conformant _meta and expects a result carrying a supportedVersions array and a capabilities object. Servers MUST implement server/discover; it replaces the initialize handshake and is the first response the suite trusts. Over HTTP a 429 on it is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s), and the answer that exchange settles on is the one this rule, its lifecycle-discover-* siblings, lifecycle-jsonrpc, the capability gates and the negative probes' not-evaluable readings all judge; a resend that gets no response is server unreachable.
rules.passCriteria: server/discover with a conformant _meta returns a result carrying a supportedVersions array and a capabilities object.
rules.failCriteria: A JSON-RPC error, no response, or a result missing either field. Over HTTP a 429 is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s) and the second answer decides, for this rule, its lifecycle-discover-* siblings, lifecycle-jsonrpc, the capability gates and the negative probes alike; a resend that gets no response is server unreachable.

rules.name: supportedVersions are well-formed
rules.description: Validates supportedVersions on the discover result: non-empty, every entry a YYYY-MM-DD string. Warns when 2026-07-28 itself is absent, since the run grades that revision and the server just answered a request declaring it.
rules.passCriteria: supportedVersions is non-empty and every entry is a YYYY-MM-DD string; the absence of 2026-07-28 is reported as a warning.
rules.failCriteria: An empty array, or any entry that is not a date-shaped string.

rules.name: server/discover carries caching hints
rules.description: Checks that the discover result carries ttlMs (an integer >= 0) and cacheScope ('public' or 'private'). Servers MUST include both caching hints on every complete server/discover result; a negative or missing ttlMs or an unknown scope fails.
rules.passCriteria: The server/discover result carries ttlMs as an integer >= 0 and cacheScope equal to public or private.
rules.failCriteria: Either field missing, ttlMs negative or non-integer, or an unknown cacheScope value.

rules.name: Response is valid JSON-RPC 2.0
rules.description: Validates the discover response envelope: jsonrpc is exactly '2.0', the id is echoed, and exactly one of result (an object) or error is present. All MCP messages MUST follow JSON-RPC 2.0 and a result response MUST include a result field. Over HTTP the setup server/discover it reads is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s) when it draws a 429, and the answer that exchange settles on is judged (a pass then adds '; resent once after HTTP 429'); a resend that gets no response is server unreachable. The envelope of a discover answered without a result is judged only when the server wrote it: a 401, a 403 that reads as an auth refusal, any other 403 (it refused the conformant request itself, so nothing is left to compare it with; the message is quoted when it names Host/Origin validation), a 429 still a 429 after the resend, or a 5xx carrying none of -32600, -32601, -32602, -32020, -32021 or -32022 fails as not evaluable, because a gateway's envelope (its -32001 on a 401, echoing the id) proves nothing about the server's JSON-RPC. A 5xx carrying one of those codes is the server's own refusal and is credited, with a warning that a 4xx is expected. Over stdio every answer is the server's.
rules.passCriteria: The server/discover response has jsonrpc exactly '2.0', the request id echoed, and exactly one of result (an object) or error. Over HTTP the setup server/discover that every lifecycle rule reads is resent once after Retry-After (capped at 2 s) when it draws a 429, and the answer it settles on is judged (the details add '; resent once after HTTP 429'); a server's own refusal code (-32600, -32601, -32602, -32020, -32021 or -32022) on a 5xx passes with a warning that a 4xx is expected.
rules.failCriteria: A missing or wrong jsonrpc field, a missing id, both or neither of result/error, or a non-object result. Over HTTP a discover answered without a result fails as not evaluable when something in front of the server wrote the envelope: a 401, any 403 (an auth gate's, or one that refused the conformant request itself, so no twin is sent; a message naming Host/Origin validation is quoted), a 429 still a 429 after its one resend, or a 5xx without one of those codes (this rule's probe is the conformant request, so a 5xx on it is not read as the server failing on a defect). A resend that gets no response is server unreachable.

rules.name: Response id matches request id
rules.description: Verifies the id on the discover response equals the id the suite sent. Result and error responses MUST include the same id as the request they answer; the suite issues numeric ids from 1000 upward so a stale or fabricated id is easy to spot.
rules.passCriteria: The id on the server/discover response equals the id the suite sent.
rules.failCriteria: A different, missing, or null id.

rules.name: Supports string request ids
rules.description: Sends server/discover with a string id and expects the response to echo it byte-for-byte as a string, on HTTP and stdio alike. Requests MUST carry a string or integer id and the server MUST return the same one; coercing '42' to 42 or dropping the id fails.
rules.passCriteria: A server/discover sent with a string id is answered with the identical string id.
rules.failCriteria: The id is coerced to a number, replaced, or dropped.

rules.name: Returns capabilities object
rules.description: Checks that the discover result has a capabilities object and that each declared feature (tools, resources, prompts, completions, logging, experimental, extensions) is itself an object. An empty {} is valid; a capability declared as true or a string is not, because sub-features such as listChanged live inside it.
rules.passCriteria: The server/discover result has a capabilities object and every declared feature is itself an object (an empty {} is valid).
rules.failCriteria: capabilities missing or not an object, or a feature declared as a boolean, string, or other non-object.

rules.name: Includes serverInfo in _meta
rules.description: Looks for result._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] on the discover result and checks it carries string name and version fields. Servers SHOULD include serverInfo on every result so a client can identify them without connection state; the report's serverInfo comes from here.
rules.passCriteria: result._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] on the server/discover result carries string name and version fields.
rules.failCriteria: serverInfo absent from _meta, or name or version missing or not strings.

rules.name: Instructions field is valid
rules.description: If the discover result includes instructions, verifies it is a string. Instructions are optional natural-language guidance for the model on how to use the server; absence passes and any other type fails.
rules.passCriteria: instructions is absent from the server/discover result, or present as a string.
rules.failCriteria: instructions is present with a non-string type.

rules.name: Rejects request without _meta
rules.description: Sends server/discover with params carrying no _meta at all (on HTTP the headers are still correct). protocolVersion and clientCapabilities are required on every request, so the request is malformed and the server MUST reject it with -32602 Invalid params; on HTTP the status MUST be 400. A rejection with a different code is reported as a warning; a result fails, because the server is inferring version and capabilities from nowhere. On HTTP, a bare 400 with no JSON-RPC error body (an intermediary answering with a status alone) passes with a warning; any other status without a JSON-RPC error body -- a 404, a 422, a plain-text 500 -- fails, since the spec requires -32602 on HTTP 400. Runs late, after the feature tests and before the security tests: a dual-era stdio server that is still deciding its era treats a claim-less message as a legacy opening, and by then a modern request has pinned the process (a --only run that skipped the feature tests sends one first on stdio -- the first declared list, else ping); the security rate-limit burst comes afterwards so an intermediary it trips cannot answer this probe. Not evaluable -- and failed -- when the conformant server/discover was itself rejected, since the rejection then proves nothing about the missing _meta, and likewise when the answer is a transport-level status (401, 403, 413, 415 or 429: an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter answering before the JSON-RPC layer read the request).
rules.passCriteria: A server/discover with no params._meta draws a JSON-RPC error (HTTP 400 on HTTP), credited only when the conformant server/discover was served and the answer is not a transport-level status (a server that rejects everything, or a 401/403/413/415/429 from an auth gate, size limit, media-type gate or rate limiter, fails as not evaluable); code -32602 is expected and any other code is reported as a warning. Runs after the feature tests and before the security tests, so a dual-era stdio server is already pinned modern (a --only run on stdio sends the first declared list, else ping, first) and the rate-limit burst cannot have tripped an intermediary.
rules.failCriteria: A result is returned, on HTTP the error arrives with a status other than 400 or no JSON-RPC error body arrives on a status other than 400 (a bare 400 passes with a warning), the conformant server/discover was itself rejected or unanswered, or the answer is a transport-level status (401, 403, 413, 415, 429) -- the last two not evaluable.

rules.name: Rejects _meta without protocolVersion
rules.description: Sends server/discover whose _meta carries clientCapabilities and clientInfo but no protocolVersion (on HTTP the MCP-Protocol-Version header is present and correct). The field is required, so the server MUST answer -32602 Invalid params and, on HTTP, status 400. A rejection with another code (-32020 is the common one) passes with a warning; a result fails.
